concepts.title: Population Density in Cities
concepts.definition: Cities crowd many people onto small land: population density - persons per square kilometre - runs far higher in cities like Gurugram than in villages such as Asadpur Khera in Haryana, and this density drives both the energy and the strains of urban life.
concepts.key_idea: People per square kilometre is the yardstick of crowding - and cities pack thousands.
concepts.textbook_ref: hees207.txt lines 63-105 (population density in cities, village vs city example)
question_patterns: what is population density and how is it calculated
compare the population density of a village and a city
find the density of a city with given population and area
why do cities have much higher population density than villages
what problems does high density bring to a city
how does density change from Gurugram city to a Haryana village

solution_steps.explain: Persons per square kilometre measure the crowding of a place.

concepts.title: Why Cities Grow: Centres of Work and Hope
concepts.definition: Cities attract people because they concentrate jobs, factories, offices, schools, hospitals and markets - offering something for everybody, as the chapter's epigraph puts it - so migration from villages keeps feeding urban growth.
concepts.key_idea: Jobs and services pull migrants in: cities grow because opportunity concentrates there.
concepts.textbook_ref: hees207.txt lines 2-62 (cities provide something for everybody), 106-128 (how cities become centres)
question_patterns: why do people migrate from villages to cities
what makes a city a centre of economic activity
list the services that cities provide better than villages
how does industry help a city grow
explain the push and pull factors of urban migration
why are cities said to provide something for everybody

solution_steps.explain: Employment, education and healthcare draw migrants to cities.
Rural joblessness and shrinking farmland push people out.
More people attract more businesses, which attract still more people.

concepts.title: Urbanisation: The Process and Its Challenges
concepts.definition: Urbanisation is the rising share of people living in urban places; as India urbanises, cities strain under slums, housing shortages, traffic, pollution and unequal services, needing planned infrastructure and governance to stay liveable.
concepts.key_idea: Urbanisation is inevitable - planning decides whether cities become engines or slums.
question_patterns: what is urbanisation
list the challenges faced by Indian cities
why do slums grow in big cities
how can cities be made more liveable
what is the role of municipal government in a city
explain traffic and pollution problems of urban areas

solution_steps.explain: Urbanisation measures the growing urban share of population.
Housing, water, transport and pollution top the urban challenge list.
Master plans, municipal services and citizen participation keep cities liveable.

concepts.title: The World's Most Populous Cities
concepts.definition: Giant cities now span the globe - Tokyo, Delhi, Shanghai and other metropolises hold tens of millions, with New Delhi among the world's most populous cities and Seoul in South Korea another megacity - showing that urbanisation is a worldwide phenomenon.
concepts.key_idea: Megacities of tens of millions now anchor the world economy - and its congestion.
concepts.textbook_ref: hees207.txt lines 129-160 (world's most populous cities in 2025, New Delhi, Seoul)
question_patterns: name the most populous cities of the world
where does New Delhi stand among world cities by population
what is a megacity
compare the growth of Tokyo and Delhi
why do megacities grow in developing countries
what problems are common to the world's largest cities

solution_steps.explain: Lists of 2025 place Asian megacities like Tokyo, Delhi and Shanghai on top.
The biggest urban agglomerations cluster in Asia.
Transport, housing and pollution solutions must match megacity scale.
